question.text: An investment adviser continues to operate without addressing a SEBI compliance notice for 45 days. Under Section 15EB of the SEBI Act, what is the maximum penalty that can be imposed for this 45-day continuing violation?

answer.text: Rs. 46 lakh (Rs. 1 lakh minimum + Rs. 1 lakh x 45 days)
Rs. 1 crore (the maximum cap applies regardless of the number of days)
Rs. 1.45 crore (Rs. 1 lakh minimum + Rs. 1 lakh per day x 45 days + additional fine)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 15EB, the penalty may extend to Rs. 1 lakh for each day during which the failure continues, subject to an overall maximum of Rs. 1 crore. For 45 days, the source-supported maximum is therefore 45 x Rs. 1 lakh = Rs. 45 lakh — well within the Rs. 1 crore cap. The Trap: Rs. 1 crore is the overall cap only once the per-day accrual reaches it (i.e., after 100 days). Quoting Rs. 1 crore for a 45-day breach ignores the per-day calculation and overstates the source-supported maximum. Note: Section 15EB has two components — a per-day amount of up to Rs. 1 lakh and an overall maximum of Rs. 1 crore. For shorter breaches, the per-day calculation drives the maximum; the Rs. 1 crore cap binds only for very long breaches.
